envelope.text: ADOPT-BOUNDED: nano-ros's options carry reserved bytes only, not rcl's `qos`,

why: ADOPTED 2026-10-28 (phase-515 C6, maintainer choice "adopt, all six"): `rcl_publisher_get_options` returns a pointer to the options the handle was initialised with, held ON the handle -- all zero for an init without options, NULL for a NULL or unusable handle, as rcl returns NULL for an invalid one. ENVELOPE (stated on the declaration): nano-ros's options struct is not rcl's -- rcl_publisher_options_t carries reserved bytes only, so the readback is the struct the caller passed (or all zero); rcl's `qos`, `allocator` and rmw-specific options are not members, so a ported `->qos` fails to compile rather than reading a wrong value, and the handle's QoS stays the one it was created with. Cost: the options struct moves onto the handle, replacing the copied `sched_context_id` where there was one (measured in the phase doc's C6 note). Test: `packages/api/nros-c/tests/run/entity_get_options.c` (`just check c`). PRIOR ROW: reads back the options a publisher was created with. `rcl_publisher_options_t` ships (`nros_generated.h:2467-2474`) and `rclc_publisher_init_with_options` takes it; what is missing is the READBACK -- nothing retains the struct on the handle and no `*_get_options` exists anywhere in our C surface, for any entity. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): this row said there is no runtime options struct. Seven ship and the correlator buckets all fourteen items `same` -- `nros_{node,publisher,subscription,service,client,action_client,action_server}_options_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/rclc/detail/nros_generated.h:1461,1729,2011,2474,2537,2556,2592`) plus a `*_get_default_options` for each, and `rcl_node_options_t::domain_id_override` is a RUNTIME per-node domain. What is genuinely absent is the LIFECYCLE around one: no `*_options_copy`, no `*_options_fini`, and no `*_get_options` readback anywhere in the C surface.
